## 2026-10-27 — Generic signaling.v1 spec draft (replaces calling-shaped RTC)

**Spec draft only.** It adds the new [signaling](docs/spec/signaling.md) spec, revision 0, and a status note at the top of [rtc-signaling](docs/spec/rtc-signaling.md). No code changed and no tests were run. There was no commit. Nothing in the draft is implemented. The local code still implements `rtc-signaling.v1` behind flags that are all off. Every decision below is **provisional** (coordinator), not signed off by the owner.

**Owner direction (2026-10-27, verbatim):** "I only intended for a general signaling mechanism, app to app, user to user, provider to provider, etc; something flexible enough for all use cases, but I didn't intend to build actual calling into bindle, that's an app level concern." And: "Core bindle should be about identity, preferences, intents, and resources; a hub for connecting things together."

**Supersession:** docs/spec/rtc-signaling.md is superseded by the signaling.v1 draft, **pending sign-off**. Until sign-off it stays the reference for the flags-off code. Its only edit is the status note. docs/architecture/rtc-signaling.md and the pending-signoffs digest were not updated.

**Design in brief:**
- **The channel.** `signaling.v1` is a signed session channel with profiles: `webrtc` (Annex A) and `data` (bounded, opaque, post-claim only). It has one feature, one exclusive slot with `consumers: ["application","provider"]`, and the unchanged `ice-relay/v1` slot.
- **Kinds and routing.** What a session is for is an intent kind with a `session` member. Invites go to the owner's chosen handler app for that kind. There is no `rtc-purpose` kind, no AMD-X1, and no cross-app visibility.
- **No calling concepts in the provider.** Its only presentation is provider-source activity items: held, no handler, unanswered. Interruption is activity notification policy. "Open in app" is an intents handoff.
- **Admission and links.** Admission is `self`, a contact link with owner-side signaling configuration, or `none`. The ticket link type is dropped, and callbacks are one-use, principal-bound contact links.
- **Security and privacy carried over:**
  - end-to-end leg-key signatures;
  - the uniform `202` with no presence oracle;
  - admission before reach, and first claim;
  - no address or candidate before the claim, with the SDP and candidate rules and IP policy in the WebRTC annex;
  - ordering and replay;
  - live approval checks, and links dying with their app;
  - principal and provider blocks;
  - separate own-device and principal-bound windows, and cheap checks first;
  - silent ends on every pre-claim path;
  - the same-host `iss` refusal;
  - deletion, moves and export.
- **Guardrails:** no offline delivery, a 120 s answer window, a 24 h cap, delete after delivery, no history, no multi-party.
- **Traceability.** Appendix A maps each RTC fix to its new section. Appendix B lists every RTC-n, RTCabc, RTCd, RTCe, RTCs, RTCf, RTCg, RTCi and RTCw item and AMD-* as kept, changed or dropped.
- **Migration plan.** Appendix C covers files, flags, tests and storage families. No data migration is needed: the flags have no env default and appear in no config, and rows exist only in local development stores.
- **Findings recorded:**
  - `rtc/block-iss/` (provider blocks) is neither exported nor excluded in `packages/runtime/export-contributors.mjs`. This is pre-existing and not fixed here.
  - The bug hunt round 3 finding R1 (no revision on owner settings) is carried into the draft as compare-and-swap.

**Decisions (provisional; each needs the owner's sign-off):**
- SG-1: a generic channel with profiles. `webrtc` is first, then `data`. Reviewer ___ Date ___ Outcome ___
- SG-2: session kinds are intent kinds, and invites route to the owner's chosen handler (AMD-SG-I1). The slim `signaling-purpose` kind with AMD-X1 was evaluated and rejected (spec §19.1); it stays the fallback. Reviewer ___ Date ___ Outcome ___
- SG-3: kind authorization is a session handler approval in intents memory, checked live and locally. The routing handler is the default, else the sole approved handler, else the activity chooser. Reviewer ___ Date ___ Outcome ___
- SG-4: provider presentation only through activity items (AMD-SG-A1). Held and unanswered items are never interruptive. Reviewer ___ Date ___ Outcome ___
- SG-5: admission through contact links with owner-side configuration (AMD-SG-L1). Tickets are dropped, and `mint_link` is interim. Reviewer ___ Date ___ Outcome ___
- SG-6: application and provider consumers. Provider features act as built-in handlers for an entity. Reviewer ___ Date ___ Outcome ___
- SG-7: the guardrails and caps (`data` ≤ 8 KiB per message and 1 MiB per leg; `seq` ≤ 4,095). Reviewer ___ Date ___ Outcome ___
- SG-8: AMD-RI1 to RI5, RV2 and RW2, and the per-entity-enablement rule, applied to the text. Reviewer ___ Date ___ Outcome ___
- SG-9: the abuse limit kinds, including the own-device, principal-bound and same-host windows, the pending reserve, cheap checks first, and per-app caps and quotas. Reviewer ___ Date ___ Outcome ___
- SG-10: principal and provider blocks with the own-entity exemption. Mutes are dropped for activity rules, scoped to the asserting provider. Reviewer ___ Date ___ Outcome ___
- SG-11: SAS out of core. Fingerprint binding kept, and `media` only as a `webrtc` parameter. Reviewer ___ Date ___ Outcome ___
- SG-12: the initiator's app origin is disclosed, as "reported by" for foreign providers (RTC-17). Reviewer ___ Date ___ Outcome ___
- SG-13: decline reasons `declined` and `unsupported`. `busy` is dropped. Reviewer ___ Date ___ Outcome ___
- SG-14: `ice-relay/v1` unchanged, with AMD-RL1 and the RTC-f rules. Reviewer ___ Date ___ Outcome ___
- SG-15: new identifiers rather than reusing `rtc-signaling.v1`. Reviewer ___ Date ___ Outcome ___
- SG-16: auto-connect as an owner setting per app and per `self` kind, same `client_id` only. Reviewer ___ Date ___ Outcome ___

**Proposed amendments (unsigned; none applied to its target document):**
- AMD-SG-I1 (intents: session kinds, session handler approvals, addressed delivery, session handoff). Written in full in spec §20.1. intents.md is not edited.
- AMD-SG-A1 (activity: provider-feature source items).
- AMD-SG-L1 (links: signaling configuration and delivery-off contact parents). It depends on the links §6 re-scope.
- AMD-SG-K1, P1, E1 and N1, which replace AMD-R1 to R3 and add a notifications rule.
- Proposed withdrawal of AMD-X1 (extensions §13; extensions.md is not edited), AMD-R4, AMD-R5 and AMD-RW1.

**Questions for the owner:** spec §19.3, items 1 to 8.

## 2026-10-27 — signaling.v1 spec rev 1 (review fixes)

**Spec revision only.** [signaling](docs/spec/signaling.md) moves from revision 0 to revision 1. It answers an independent review of revision 0, and folds in owner direction that arrived during the revision. No code changed and no tests were run. There was no commit. Only docs/spec/signaling.md and this entry were edited: intents.md, links.md, activity.md, notifications.md and security.md are not edited, and their changes stay proposed amendments in spec §20. Every decision is **provisional** (coordinator) and unsigned. The owner said provisional decisions may be adopted for now without sign-off. They are adopted on that basis, and sign-off stays blank.

**Owner direction during the revision (2026-10-27, relayed by the coordinator):**
1. The foundation stays: the signed channel, admission, claim, the WebRTC annex and relay. Calling and use semantics move to the app layer. The messaging app (Parlay) implements calling: a call invite is a message with a JSON media type, specified in the messaging/BindleBox spec. Presentational parts, including the "no handler" activity item, go, or shrink to a minimal hook.
2. Intents as the handoff is right in principle, but may not fit every case. There are probably two establishment modes: (a) invite-style, a user-facing request that an app surfaces; (b) always-on, where own endpoints or pre-authorised peers wire up when an app opens (for example agent daemons and a phone remote-control interface). This needs a spike. Intents routing is not final.
3. Intents routing needs a robust short-list: likely candidates first, an expansion to all capable apps, and confirm-only with one candidate. This is an intents requirement.

**How the owner direction was applied:**
- **Presentation (spec §11.3).** Signaling creates no activity items. AMD-SG-A1 and AMD-SG-N1 are withdrawn. What remains is a minimal **owner hook**: an owner-only list of held invites and invites with no eligible endpoint. It holds minimal facts, never interrupts, notifies or pushes, is deleted by `answer_by`, and offers hand off, dismiss (silent), block and allow-later.
- **Establishment modes (spec §5.6, §19.1, §19.4).** Intents routing is marked the leading candidate for mode (a), provisional. Mode (b) is described as a separate path, with the rev 1 mechanisms that approach it (own-entity `target`, auto-connect, standing acceptance, principal-bound links, separate windows). It lists the questions the spike must answer. No mode (b) path may be added before the spike. Spike questions S1 and S2.
- **Chooser short-list (spec §20.1.11).** Written as an intents requirement amending intents §7.3 for every chooser, not as a signaling rule.

**Review findings and resolutions:**
- **H1** (the user-action rule blocks provider features, service entities, headless servers and conferencing). Added **standing acceptance**: an owner setting per (handler, kind) for cross-entity kinds, off by default. Its page must disclose that it makes the entity's availability visible to any admitted initiator. Provider features accept only under it, within their declared policy. Spec §4.1–§4.3, §5.5, §10.3 `standing_accept`, §20.1.4.
- **H2** (`data` cost and scope). Caps are 4 KiB per message and 64 KiB per leg. `data` is a message type of the `data` profile only, never in `webrtc` sessions. An aggregate per-entity `data` byte budget is a required limit kind. Replay state keeps only payload hashes. A production gate needs the enforced budget, a cost-model row, and the custody statement reconciled. **AMD-SG-S1** (§20.9) is the proposed security.md "Trust boundaries" sentence on hosted signaling copies. **Reference discrepancy:** the review cited security.md "around line 224", but security.md has 85 lines. The hosted-copy position is the security.md "Trust boundaries" paragraph (plaintext trust under v0) together with DEVLOG 2026-10-12 line 224 ("Direct WebRTC data channels avoid hosted payload copies"). AMD-SG-S1 reconciles both. The cost-model row is still to be written (code). Spec §1.2, §3.5, §7.2, §7.3, §9.2, §13.1.
- **H3** (AMD-SG-L1 underspecified and in conflict with links §6). Split it:
  - **L1a (now):** owner-side configuration on existing contact parents, replacing `rtc/contact/`. It is **forbidden on conditional parents**, rather than evaluating audience policy against the certificate principal. Reasons: policy evaluation would put host policy, and the unwired links §7.3 foreign path, into federation verification; its per-principal-day quota does not map to `uses`; and `principal` already gives an exact local alternative. The links §6.3 representation, the composer and the previews are unchanged and disclose nothing.
  - **L1b (deferred, unavailable):** `mint_link`, minted and signaling-only parents, delivery-off and callbacks.
  - Spec §5.3, §10.2, §20.3.
- **M1.** `claim` accept and `mint_link` are added to the live-approval list. A decline stays ungated. Spec §10.1.
- **M2.** Narrowing revokes only parents whose `minted_by` is that app. Owner-configured parents lose the kind and are never revoked, and an empty configuration is removed. **Reading added:** the kind is removed only when no approved handler for it remains, because otherwise invites still route to the remaining handler. Spec §14.2 step 5.
- **M3.** Callback verification is written into deferred §20.3.2:
  - the link is canonical and its digest matches;
  - its owner equals the verified initiator origin principal, and otherwise the callback is dropped silently;
  - retention at both providers is defined;
  - the callback is revoked on an unclaimed end and counted in the per-app quota.
- **M4.** When a second handler is approved and no default exists, the sole handler is promoted to the explicit default in the same transaction. The page says so and offers the switch. Spec §20.1.5.
- **M5.** A recipient resolves kind versions only from its store, a mirror, or a background fetch whose triggering does not depend on recipient state. Spec §3.4, §9.2 step 7.
- **M6.** The spec states that AMD-SG-I1 adds an authority record to intents, and writes explicit amendments to intents §1, §5 and §9.5. For organization entities, a person authorized through the owner interface approves (organizations §6.3). For hosted service entities, whoever operates that entity's owner interface approves. Spec §4.3, §20.1, §20.1.4, §20.1.10.
- **M7.** Appendix C now has:
  - the lifecycle hooks: approval removal or clearing, and a connection ending, call §14.2. They replace `narrowBoundOptions` and the grant-changed path;
  - the `intent-choices` export fields;
  - `SIGNALING_ENABLED` requiring `INTENT_APP_HANDLERS_ENABLED`. **Deviation:** the `ACTIVITY_V2_ENABLED` requirement the review asked for is dropped, because under the owner's later direction signaling creates no activity items. It returns only if an activity mirror is adopted.
- **M8.** Superseded by the owner direction: there are no activity items. The owner hook never interrupts, folds foreign initiators per issuer (local ones per principal), and labels the chooser as triggered by an incoming request. Spec §11.3, §11.4.
- **M9.** Moot for signaling, which creates no items. A system evidence profile, plus a provider-feature source, is written as the precondition for any later activity mirror. Spec §20.2.
- **L1.** `target` is restricted to the initiating app's own endpoints. Spec §5.4, §10.2.
- **L2.** Glare auto-accept requires the surviving invite to be within the endpoint's own outgoing one: the same kind line and profile, with params within. Spec §8.3.
- **L3.** Endpoints MUST NOT put addresses in `context`, and providers cannot enforce it. The overclaims in §1.2 item 6 and §12.3 are fixed. Spec §1.2, §7.2, §12.3.
- **L4.** Own-entity `open` calls count against the `self` window, not `opens`. This is a **code change**: today `opens` (60/h) binds before `self` (120/h). The principal-bound windows are aligned with `inviteLimits` (`pair`, `caller`, `issuerParent`, `preferred`). Spec §13.1, Appendix B RTC-11, C.1.
- **L5.** Support for session kinds and approvals is a local requirement. The `intent-links.v1` dependency is removed from the feature row, and peers never check it. Spec §3.1, §20.1.8, §20.5.
- **L6.** Each routing case fixes a handoff target. An own-entity invite whose approved initiating app has no eligible endpoint hands off to that app. Spec §5.4.
- **L7.** The drain-rate residual for dark batches is recorded, with a SHOULD to pace dark drops. It is not closed. Spec §9.2.
- **L8.** New normative rule: no relay credential without a per-owner byte cap enforced from the relay provider's usage data. **AMD-SG-S2** (§20.9) is the proposed security.md gate. Spec §16.7.
- **L9.** §9.2 step 2 now only verifies the link, with no fetch and no spend. Configuration is evaluated at step 7 and the use spent at step 8. The colliding-offers rule is restored in §16.6.
- **L10.** Appendix C adds the following, and spec §12.6 states the `rtc/block-iss/` export gap and requires the new block family to be exported:
  - `apps/node/resources.mjs` and `apps/worker/objects.mjs` (`RTC_BOUND_CHECK`, `RTC_EGRESS`, `RTC_FOREIGN_ISSUERS`);
  - `apps/worker/federation.mjs` and `apps/worker/index.mjs` (`rtcOccupant`);
  - `packages/runtime/routes/index.mjs` and `packages/runtime/account/index.mjs`;
  - `scripts/cost-model.mjs`;
  - the two test helpers;
  - `apps/web/styles.css`;
  - the `rtc/inbound` limiter scope.

**Provisional answers to the rev 0 owner questions (spec §19.3; unsigned):**
1. Intents routing (A), with M4 and M6. B stays the documented fallback. Narrowed by the later owner direction: A is the leading candidate for mode (a) only, pending the spike.
2. Never interrupt by default, and drop "unanswered". "Held" and "no handler" are kept. Under the later owner direction they survive only as owner-hook entries, and the provider never interrupts at all.
3. `mint_link` and callbacks are unavailable until the links re-scope, with no interim ticket type. Owner-side configuration on existing parents ships now, with the H3 audience fix.
4. `data` is acceptable with the H2 changes.
5. The media bound is dropped. Only the structural `m=` type check (audio, video, application) remains.
6. Disclose the app origin, labelled "reported by" for foreign initiators.
7. The uniform 404 for an unknown identity.
8. A hosted service entity is enough for provider to provider, given H1.

**New provisional decisions:** SG-17 (standing acceptance), SG-18 (no configuration on conditional parents), SG-19 (kind resolution sources), SG-20 (`target`, glare and the handoff target), SG-21 (two establishment modes; mode (b) waits for the spike) and SG-22 (the intents chooser short-list as an intents requirement). SG-1 to SG-16 are revised in place in spec §19.2. Each needs sign-off.

**Still open (spec §19.4):**
- S1: do intents fit every mode (a) case?
- S2: the shape of mode (b);
- I3: a vendor's native and web clients under different `client_id`s. Grouping by verified registrable domain, as intents §7.4 does for exclusions, is one option;
- the timing of the links §6 re-scope, for L1b;
- whether to accept the drain-rate residual and the unenforceable `context` address rule.

Also still to do: the cost-model `data` row and the aggregate budget's reference value, and code for everything (nothing is implemented to this text). docs/architecture/rtc-signaling.md and the pending-signoffs digest are not updated.

## 2026-10-27 — Owner direction: core scope, Parlay, signaling consumers

**Owner direction (recorded by the coordinator, 2026-10-27; the decisions listed under "provisional" below are unsigned).**
- **Core Bindle** is identity, preferences, intents, resources and hub connectivity. Event buses stay in core.
- **Messaging** comes out of core entirely and moves into the messaging app, kept in this monorepo for now.
  - The 3sln.me email auto-response to 3sln.me addresses stays (free marketing). When the messaging app fills the intake slot, mail is forwarded to it.
- **Calling** is app-level and belongs to the messaging app.
  - A call invite is an ordinary message with a JSON media type: audio and/or video, and it expires.
  - The existing RTC call-handling work moves into the app rather than being discarded.
  - The 3sln.me notification layer gains an opportunistic, never-guaranteed ringing-style notification that apps can request.
- **Generic signaling stays** as a foundation, with two kinds of consumers:
  - invite-style (the messaging app's calls);
  - always-on, auto-wiring (for example a fleet of agent harness daemons, enrolled by QR/device sign-in and remote-controlled from a phone).
  - How sessions are established in each mode needs a spike.
- **Intents** are the handoff mechanism. Routing must show a short list of likely candidates, expandable to every capable app; a single candidate only needs confirming.
- **Organizations plus relations** become one cohesive extension spec if they can be cleanly sharded; otherwise they stay together in core.
- **The commands/automation system** (apps contribute commands; the provider exposes them as MCP, user commands, etc.) becomes an extension. Providers declare the extensions they support in their manifest.
- **The activity feed** is a 3sln.me feature, not a Bindle spec.
- **The email bridge's placement** needs a spike.

**Naming.**
- The spec name "Bindle Messaging" is the user's decision of 2026-10-20 (see that entry).
- The app name "Parlay" is used by the owner and adopted provisionally. The earlier clash notes still apply ("Parley" is taken by existing messaging products; "Parlay" reads as a betting term).
- The mechanical rename of the BindleBox spec, apps/bindlebox, the bindlebox-* packages and the BINDLEBOX_* flags (retired as aliases) is folded into the messaging tear-out.

**Provisional (coordinator), unsigned:**
- The messaging tear-out removes code first and leaves existing message rows in storage, inert. Deleting that data is the separate, irreversible BB-CUT reset, and still requires explicit owner confirmation (SQ-1).
- **User decision (2026-10-27), SQ-1 confirmed:** "Confirmed, drop the data, nobody is actually using 3sln.me yet; destructive cleanup is fine for now." The BB-CUT message-data reset is authorised. The tear-out may delete legacy messaging rows (messages, contacts, conversations, blocks) instead of leaving them inert.
- Saved contacts move with the messaging app (SQ-2), provisionally.

Spikes in progress:
- docs/architecture/signaling-modes-spike.md
- docs/architecture/extension-catalogue-spike.md

## 2026-10-27 — signaling.v1 spec rev 2 (offer and pairing bases)

**Spec revision only.** [signaling](docs/spec/signaling.md) moves from revision 1 to revision 2. It applies the [establishment-modes spike](docs/architecture/signaling-modes-spike.md) (2026-10-27): change requests CR-1 to CR-13 and decisions SMS-1 to SMS-8. Only docs/spec/signaling.md and this entry were edited. No code changed, no tests were run, and there was no commit. intents.md, device-authorization.md, messaging.md, activity.md, links.md and security.md are not edited: their changes stay proposed amendments or references in spec §20. Every decision is **provisional** (coordinator) and unsigned. The owner allowed provisional adoption without sign-off, so the decisions are adopted on that basis and sign-off stays blank.

**Source decisions, all provisional and unsigned (spike §5):**
- **SMS-1.** One signaling mechanism with explicit establishment bases. No second mechanism.
- **SMS-2.** Invite-style establishment is a reverse dial using a principal-bound, single-use `offer`, carried in an app-level invitation. Callbacks and `callback_digest` are withdrawn.
- **SMS-3.** Always-on establishment is an owner `pairing` record. Own-entity, it extends `self`; cross-entity, it is the relation basis. Standing acceptance is limited to provider features and service entities.
- **SMS-4.** Headless clients enroll through device authorization. The approval page may offer a pairing bound to the new client session.
- **SMS-5.** Intents route viewer-initiated handoffs only. Incoming events never use the chooser.
- **SMS-6.** The chooser shows a ranked short list from owner-local and verified signals, with one action to expand, and a confirm page for a single candidate.
- **SMS-7.** Ringing is an advisory presentation hint, with delivery policy and fallback in 3sln.me, and is never guaranteed.
- **SMS-8.** Parlay's call invite is a Bindle Messaging message with `application/vnd.bindle.messaging.call-invite+json` (the spike's current identifier, after the concurrent rename).

**What changed in the spec:**
- **Bases (spec §5.2, §5.6).** Admission gains `offer` and `pairing` beside `self`, `link` and `none`. Each basis fixes admission, routing and acceptance (summary table in §5.6). S1 and S2 are answered (§19.4).
- **`offer` basis (spec §5.7; CR-1, CR-2).**
  - New methods: `offer` (widening; 1 to 16 principals, 10 to 900 s) and `revoke_offer` (narrowing).
  - The wire carries `offer_digest`, with the token in a new batch `offers` member.
  - The offer is checked at step 7 and spent atomically at step 8, only when its principal equals the verified leg principal. A wrong principal admits nothing and spends nothing.
  - Offers are stored hashed, never delivered to endpoints, and excluded from export.
  - `callback_digest` and the callback design are removed. The offer is carried inside an app message, and the minting app claims automatically.
- **Pairing record (spec §5.8; CR-5).**
  - Members: `id`, `revision`, `kind`, `local`, `peer`, `accept: "auto"`, `label`, `created_via`, `expires_at`.
  - Created by owner action only. It stays pending until the approvals exist.
  - Own-entity, it extends `self` across apps, which solves I3. Cross-entity, it is `{"relation": "pairing"}`, and both owners' records are required.
  - Revoked by removal, by clearing the approval or grant, or by revoking the bound client session. Exported as owner data.
- **Routing (spec §5.4; CR-3).** Case 4 (offer: the minting endpoint, else the minting app) and case 5 (pairing: the paired app, narrowed to the bound client session). Neither has a handoff. **Reading added:** an own-entity pairing invite must name `target`, so that each invite still reaches exactly one app.
- **Acceptance (spec §5.5, §10.3; CR-4, CR-11).** The projection gains `offer_match` and `paired`. Standing acceptance is restricted to provider features and service entities. Different apps of the owner auto-connect only under an explicit own-entity pairing. Grouping by registrable domain is not used for signaling.
- **Kind `bases` (spec §3.4, §20.1.1; CR-6).** An optional, frozen subset, enforced by both providers.
- **Discovery (spec §10.2; CR-7).** `endpoints({pairing})` returns own-entity paired endpoints with `client_id`, never across entities.
- **Limits (spec §13.1; CR-8).**
  - Offer invites are bounded by their offer.
  - Reference values: 64 live offers per entity, 120 mints per app per hour, and a pairing window of 30 per hour per (pairing, endpoint pair), with at most two live sessions.
  - Both join the pending reserve.
  - **Reading added:** offer invites still count against the per-(initiator, recipient) window, and a wrong or unknown offer counts as an unbased invite.
- **Glare (spec §8.3; CR-9).** It also covers crossing pairing invites.
- **Owner hook and handoff (spec §11.3, §11.4; CR-10).** They never apply to `offer` or `pairing` invites.
- **Daemon enrolment (spec §5.9).**
  - Headless clients enroll through device authorization, with code entry by default and a QR code optional.
  - **Finding:** device authorization §7 item 4 revokes a device grant when the approving browser session signs out.
  - **AMD-SG-D1** (spec §20.11, proposed, unsigned, device-authorization.md not edited): the owner may mark a standing device grant that survives sign-out and is revoked explicitly from Devices.
- **Intents scope (spec §5.6, §20.10).** Intents are for user-initiated handoff only, never for routing incoming events. The short-list requirement stays an intents amendment, **AMD-INT-R1** (replacing rev 1 §20.1.11): ranking obligations, single-candidate confirmation, the scope rule, and the `start-call` candidate kind. The choice history is **on by default and owner-deletable** (provisional).
- **Calling stays out (spec §11.3, §20.12; CR-12).** Signaling stays call-free, and §20.12 is references only:
  - the call-invite message type belongs to the Bindle Messaging spec (docs/spec/messaging.md, after the concurrent bindlebox.md rename), owned by the Parlay app;
  - the ring hint is a separate proposal on the 3sln.me notice contract (app-to-owner notices; "Bindle Notices" in the extension-catalogue spike), not signaling text.
- **Decisions and tests (spec §19, §21; CR-13).**
  - New SG-23 to SG-30. SG-2, SG-5, SG-16, SG-17, SG-20 and SG-22 are revised in place. SG-21 is superseded by SG-23.
  - Conformance tests for offers (spent once under concurrency, a wrong principal admits nothing unspent, minter routing despite a different intents default), pairings (pending until approvals, device-auth revocation ends paired sessions with `revoked`, the relation basis without a record gets the uniform `202`), `bases` enforcement, and an engine-level seeded chaos test.
- **Appendices.** A.4 maps every CR and SMS item. B updates RTC-4, RTC-11, AMD-R5, RTCd-6 and RTCg-9 to 12. C adds the pairing and offer families, the device-authorization page work, and the AMD-INT-R1 work, and reorders the plan.
- **Consistency fix.** A leftover rev 1 sentence in §5.4 ("records a 'no handler' activity item") now reads as an owner-hook entry, matching §11.3.

**Open owner questions (spec §19.5; provisional answers adopted, unsigned):**
1. Reverse dial for calls: the callee's app opens the session, and the caller's app answers automatically. Recommended: yes.
2. Pairing replaces open standing acceptance for app endpoints: yes.
3. A standing device grant survives the approving browser's sign-out (AMD-SG-D1): yes.
4. A 16-person mesh is enough for Parlay v1.
5. Choice history is on by default.
6. A ring opens the app's call screen directly. This is notice-contract scope, not signaling.
7. Parlay may not ring through its own push: all rings go through the provider.

**Still open:** the drain-rate residual and the unenforceable `context` address rule. The links §6 re-scope timing now matters only for AMD-SG-L1b (minting and delivery-off). Code for everything (nothing is implemented to this text). docs/architecture/rtc-signaling.md and the pending-signoffs digest are not updated.

## 2026-10-27 — signaling.v1 spec rev 2.1 (rev 2 review fixes)

**Spec revision only.** [signaling](docs/spec/signaling.md) moves from revision 2 to revision 2.1, answering an independent review of revision 2 (findings H1 to H4, M1 to M7, L1 to L8; spec Appendix A.5 maps each one to its fix). Only docs/spec/signaling.md and this entry were edited. No code changed, no tests were run, and there was no commit. messaging.md, intents.md, device-authorization.md and security.md are not edited. Every decision is **provisional** (coordinator) and unsigned, adopted under the owner's permission to adopt provisional decisions without sign-off. Sign-off stays blank.

**Decisions (spec §19.2; all provisional and unsigned):**
- **SG-31 Offers (H1, M1, L1 to L4).**
  - Only the minting endpoint gets `offer_match`. The minting app's other endpoints get `offer_match: false` and claim only after a user action.
  - Before any automatic claim, the endpoint MUST check that `basis.offer_digest` equals the digest of an offer token it holds outstanding, and that the verified initiator is that offer's principal. The check is keyed on the digest the app computes from its own token, not on `context`.
  - The principal is compared read-only at §9.2 step 7 and re-confirmed atomically at step 8. Limit classification follows the principal match, so a borrowed live offer counts as an unbased invite.
  - Revoking (by the app, by narrowing or by the owner) or expiring an offer silently ends the pending unclaimed sessions it admitted.
  - New: a per-app live-offer cap (reference 32), and owner controls to list and revoke live offers.
  - Key warming at `offer` is **issuer-level only**: no per-principal identity or key fetch. A per-principal fetch would leak the invitation to a third-party issuer before the invited party acts, and would amplify up to 16 times per call. A refresh lane for invites that name a live offer covers the cost.
  - Mint `expires_in` covers the invitation's remaining lifetime plus a skew margin (reference 60 s).
  - Offer tokens and the batch `offers` and `links` members are never logged.
- **SG-32 Pairings (H2, H4, M2, M3, L6).**
  - **Coverage:** `client_id` plus the endpoint's recorded client session, checked on both sides and in both roles. It applies to routing, `target`, the §5.1 item 7 initiator check, `endpoints({pairing})` and the `auto_connect`/`paired` projection.
  - **New `opens` member** (`local`, `peer`, `both`). A pairing made through device authorization defaults to the interactive app opening.
  - **`endpoints({pairing})`** answers only the opening side. It labels endpoints with the provider's Devices names, never `register` labels, and drops `last_seen` for other apps' endpoints.
  - **Deletion.** Clearing deletes a pairing; only creation yields a pending one. An approval page that would activate a pending pairing names it, and a pending pairing is deleted after 7 days. This resolves the §13.4/§14.2 inconsistency.
  - **Blocks.** A principal or provider block deletes matching pairings, ending their claimed sessions with `revoked`.
  - **Creation and moves.** Creation checks `parties`. A kind version that adds disclosure needs re-confirmation. On a move, offers and pairings are deleted at the source; an imported pairing starts pending.
- **SG-33 Pairing limits (H3).**
  - Own-entity pairings keep the per-(pairing, endpoint pair) window and the two-session cap.
  - Cross-entity pairings are keyed per pairing `id` at the recipient: 30 per hour per local covered endpoint (at most 240), and at most 2 × the local covered endpoints live.
  - A pairing sub-budget of pending, connected and `data` capacity (reference: half of each).
  - The pending reserve is split into a `self` share and a cross-entity share (offer, relation-basis pairing, principal-bound links), with a reference of 2 each.
  - The §21 test is fixed to match.
- **SG-34 Cross-entity creation, enforcement and calls (M4, L7, M7).**
  - Creation needs fresh authentication.
  - A handle is shown only under a verified binding; otherwise the full principal and issuer.
  - Wording comes from the kind's sensitivity categories.
  - Expiry is mandatory: default 90 days, at most 1 year, renewable.
  - Disclosure that against a non-conforming peer provider only the recipient's own record is enforced (this corrects the "both records required" overstatement).
  - **Recommended:** leave `pairing` out of call kinds' `bases` in v1, so that no cross-person call is answered automatically. Same-owner pairing for non-call kinds stays.
  - A call's audio/video choice lives in the app message body (the Bindle Messaging call-invite), not in signaling params. The §20.12 call kind is now valid under rev 2: `profiles: {"webrtc": {}}`, bases `["offer", "link"]`, answer `params` `{offer}`.
- **SG-35 Glare (L5).** Crossing sessions are ranked by SHA-256 over both initiator leg key thumbprints, never by the `sid` the peer chose. Equal ranks cancel both.
- **Revised in place:**
  - **SG-24, SG-25, SG-27:** cross-references to SG-31, SG-33 and SG-34.
  - **SG-28 (M5, M6):**
    - A device-authorization pairing goes live only after the owner compares a short code in the paired app. The code is derived from the client's `dpop_jkt`, and the confirmation page is reached through `approval_required`.
    - The post-approval notification names the pairing and the standing mark.
    - Providers MAY restrict which clients are offered the mark.
    - AMD-SG-D1's standing mark is exempt only from the approving session's own sign-out, its natural expiry and session-count eviction. Global sign-out, remote revocation and a credential change still revoke.
    - Devices shows last-refresh and network-change signals.
  - **SG-29 (L8, AMD-INT-R1):** choice history is scoped per (person, acting entity) and disclosed at first use. The provider's own review is removed from ranking and from the fallback order, to avoid self-preferencing. This changes the existing intents §13 consent case "once records nothing".
  - **SG-30 (M7):** the media note.

**New owner questions (spec §19.5, provisional answers adopted, unsigned):**
8. Leave `pairing` out of the call kind's bases in v1. Recommended: yes.
9. Cross-entity pairings always expire. Recommended: yes.

**Readings added (not in the review, provisional):**
- endpoints record the registering client session;
- a pairing `state` member;
- the dpop_jkt-derived confirmation code with no new method;
- no standing mark where the approval skipped code typing;
- reconnection backoff replacing the `last_seen` trigger.

**Follow-ups:**
- **docs/spec/messaging.md must align** with spec §20.12 when the call-invite §5.5 is written: no `profiles.webrtc.media` and no `params.media`, bases `["offer", "link"]`, and an invitation lifetime within the offer's skew margin. Another agent owns that file, so it was not edited.
- The intents §13 test change and the AMD-SG-D1 text apply only if those amendments are adopted.
- Still open: the drain-rate residual, the unenforceable `context` address rule, and the peer-provider residual of cross-entity pairings.
- Code for everything; the pending-signoffs digest is not updated.

## 2026-10-27 — Messaging removed from core; Parlay rename; BB-CUT reset

Owner direction: "Messaging should be entirely torn out of core"; messaging belongs to the Parlay app, built in this monorepo for now. User decision SQ-1 (2026-10-27): "Confirmed, drop the data, nobody is actually using 3sln.me yet; destructive cleanup is fine for now." Implemented locally only; nothing is deployed or production-verified. Every decision below not quoted from the user is **provisional** (coordinator) and unsigned. The RTC/signaling code, routes and UI were not edited (signaling is being redesigned separately); `docs/spec/signaling.md` was not touched.

**1. Renames (phase 1).**
- `apps/bindlebox` → `apps/parlay`; `packages/bindlebox-engine` → `packages/messaging-engine`; `packages/bindlebox-protocol` → `packages/messaging-protocol`; `tests/bindlebox` → `tests/parlay`; `scripts/bindlebox.mjs` → `scripts/parlay.mjs`; `test:bindlebox[:web]` → `test:parlay[:web]`; `tests/intents-parley.test.mjs` → `intents-parlay`, `tests/browser/intent-parley-browser.mjs` → `intent-parlay-browser`. Product name "Parlay" (owner's working name; the earlier clash notes still apply) replaces BindleBox/Parley in code, UI text (`APP_BRAND`) and docs.
- **Spec:** `docs/spec/bindlebox.md` is now **Bindle Messaging** at `docs/spec/messaging.md`. The legacy core messaging spec moved to `apps/parlay/docs/legacy/messaging.md`, beside `contact-tokens.md`, `contact-delivery.md` and `conversations.md` (moved from `docs/spec/`, each with a "retired from core" banner). They were removed from the public docs list (`scripts/public-docs.mjs`); Bindle Messaging was **not** added to it (publication decision left to the owner).
- **Wire identifiers** (nothing is published): `https://spec.bindle.example/bindlebox/v1…` → `…/messaging/v1…`; `application/vnd.bindlebox.*` → `application/vnd.bindle.messaging.*`; `bindlebox-*` signing and typ domains → `bindle-messaging-*`; app-internal `bindlebox-session|boundary|shell` → `parlay-*`; archive prefix `bindlebox/v1/` → `parlay/v1/`. The signed protocol vectors were regenerated (`tests/parlay/vectors/generate.mjs`) and the ingress slot digest pin in `apps/parlay/integration.json` updated.
- **Flags/config:** the app's `BINDLEBOX_ENABLED`, `_SERVICES`, `_EGRESS`, `_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `_CLIENT_ID`, `_ADAPTER_MODULE`, `_DATA_DIRECTORY`, `_LOCAL_TEST_KEY_HOLDER` are now `PARLAY_*`. `apps/parlay/env.mjs` (`parlayEnv`) reads the retired `BINDLEBOX_<X>` only while `PARLAY_<X>` is unset (new name wins), in the Worker entry and Durable Objects and the Node CLI. The app keeps no flag records, so the alias cannot widen a quarantined record. In the core registry nothing changed: `BINDLEBOX_ENABLED` stays in `RETIRED_FLAGS` (replacement `LINKS_ENABLED`, `envAlias` with the review-F1 quarantine rule) and no core flag names Parlay. *(Provisional: the brief asked for aliases "via registry RETIRED_FLAGS/envAlias"; the only BINDLEBOX flag in the core registry was already retired that way, and the app cannot import the core registry under its import boundary, so the app-side alias mirrors the registry rule.)*

**2. Moved (core code that was activity or links, not messaging).**

## 2026-10-27 — Device sign-in doc scope fix; local clients and pairing consent spike; Bindle/3sln.me doc split direction

**Owner direction (2026-10-27).**
- Keep Bindle specs separate from 3sln.me docs.
- Publish every spec and spec extension with the 3sln.me artefacts, so cross-references resolve.
- Fix the device sign-in docs so the confusion between them cannot recur.
- Cover every sign-in use case securely, including CLIs, daemons and local web apps (`localhost:*`, `*.localhost`). Treat these as integrations in their own right that declare their own preference fragments.
- In a pairing, every app connection needs the user's consent, not only the daemon's.

**Doc fix (applied).**
- `docs/spec/device-login.md`: the header wrongly called [device authorization](docs/spec/device-authorization.md) its "successor". It now says the doc is 3sln.me's own sign-in policy (passkeys, sessions, and session handoff to another browser, which yields a provider session) and that device authorization does not replace it.
- `docs/spec/device-authorization.md` §1: the out-of-scope bullet cross-links device-login and states the difference (provider session vs app grant).
- The wrong note came from the "Coordinator" row of `docs/architecture/linked-approval.md` §14.

**Spike.** [docs/architecture/local-clients-spike.md](docs/architecture/local-clients-spike.md), decisions LC-1 to LC-14 (provisional, unsigned):
- It separates the sign-in mechanism (M1–M6) from the use case (U1–U6).
- Local clients:
  - a per-installation DPoP key thumbprint `client_id` (RFC 9278);
  - a self-asserted local manifest, pinned at approval;
  - always shown as "unverified app on your device"; never inherits another client's approvals;
  - a 30-day idle limit;
  - a loopback code+PKCE+DPoP flow for CLIs and local web apps, with the device grant for headless clients;
  - all behind a proposed `LOCAL_CLIENTS_ENABLED` flag, default off.
- Pairing stays a per-edge owner record, under rules P1–P4: each party holds its own grant, one consent per edge, explicit activation, and the pairing is shown on both parties' rows. A slot assignment and an RPC resource were rejected (§4).
- Change requests: CR-L1 to CR-L10 against signaling.md, CR-A1 to CR-A7 against the auth docs. None is applied.
- Open owner questions: 4, each with a recommended answer (spike §6).

**Doc split (planned, not applied).** Bindle core stays in `docs/spec/`; Bindle extensions (signaling, messaging, organizations) go to `docs/spec/extensions/`; 3sln.me reference-service docs go to `docs/3sln/`; superseded specs are kept so links still resolve. Every current spec gets published under its group, with a build check against links to unpublished specs. Mixed docs (security.md, auth.md) get split. Publication currently omits 15 specs, including extensions, intents, links, events and signaling.

## 2026-10-27 — Owner direction: manifest declarations (features, slots, ref)

**Owner direction (2026-10-27).**
- `features` is the same thing as extensions, minus namespacing and atomicity: remove it.
- Anything optional is by definition an extension, not core. Core is the conformance floor plus the extension mechanism.
- No slot exists outside an extension spec. Anyone wanting a slot publishes an extension.
- Extension-level options plus per-slot options is acceptable, but question whether slots add anything over extension URL plus options.
- `ref` / local ids are not ratified without a concrete use case. Users should see useful descriptions (for example from spec metadata), never a local name.

**Coordinator analysis.**
- Current state:
  - Bindle core defines no slots. Messaging owns intake and ingress, Signaling owns signaling and ice-relay, and `item-classifier` is 3sln.me's own.
  - The extensions spec never shows `ref` to users. An earlier coordinator reply said consent shows it; that was wrong.
- What `ref` currently does:
  - lets several provider features consume one slot, carried as the `bindle.feature` credential claim;
  - gives a stable entry identity so approvals survive manifest edits;
  - lets a provider offer several built-in occupants.
- What a slot adds over a plain preference fragment:
  - owner-only assignment;
  - resource values with a cardinality rule;
  - per-consumer approval with no occupancy oracle;
  - rules on who may consume (provider features, apps or both).

**Proposal (provisional, unsigned; not applied).** Extensions revision 3:
- Remove `features` from protocol §2.
- The manifest `extensions` array becomes `{spec, options}` for providers and integrations alike, with the spec URL as the identity.
- The slot rules become a generic "assignable" marking on preference fragments, defined by extension specs and enforced generically by providers.
- No `ref`, local ids or slot list in the generic mechanism. Per-feature identity, where an extension needs it (for example separate email and SMS bridges), is defined by that extension's options schema.
- User-facing text comes from the extension spec's published metadata.
- Planned order: draft it before the signaling implementation, so signaling.v1 is built in the new shape.

## 2026-10-27 — Owner direction: remove slots; classifier scope; surfacing candidates

**Owner direction (2026-10-27).**
- Remove slots.
- Selection policy becomes a general preference-field attribute, not anything slot-specific.
- Provider features and extensions may consume fragments the way apps do.
- The classifier should be a generic AI resource: a contract for item and media classification that the messaging app uses and 3sln.me implements as a Workers AI wrapper. Message categories belong to the messaging app.
- The owner asked how the provider surfaces newly possible features or replacements without bothering the user.

**Coordinator proposals (provisional, unsigned; not applied).**
- **Email bridge to Parlay without slots:**
  - The Messaging extension publishes an `intake` fragment with one provider-consumable resource field (max 1, contract `public-intake/v1`).
  - Enabling the bridge is a grant request on that fragment. On one consent screen the owner picks among the pool resources that satisfy the contract, which sets the value and grants `deliver` on that resource only.
  - Switching apps needs re-approval. An emptied field makes the bridge hold mail and send its fixed auto-reply.
- **Classifier, current state:** a paid built-in (plans paid/plus/ultra; 200 calls a day, 2,000 a month, semantic budget ledger) wrapping Workers AI `clef-flash`. It has three problems:
  - eleven message categories and their prompts are hard-coded in the provider under the generic `decision-model/v1` name;
  - it is published as the 3sln.me `item-classifier/v1` slot;
  - core `packages/core/tags.mjs` holds a messaging classification enum.
- **Classifier, proposal:**
  - a generic `item-classification/v1` contract, where the caller supplies a bounded label set with descriptions and gets a score per label;
  - 3sln.me implements it as a paid Workers AI wrapper that keeps its untrusted-data framing;
  - remove the slot and the core enum; Parlay owns its categories.
  - Caller-supplied labels need a security review.
- **Surfacing candidates (3sln.me policy):**
  - Offer a resource in the connect flow only when an empty field has a waiting consumer, or when a disabled feature becomes possible.
  - Replacements for already-filled fields stay passive (the settings page and a collapsed "also works with").
  - Fields with no consumer are not surfaced.
  - Notify only when something in use breaks.
  - Each (field, resource) pair is asked once and a dismissal is permanent. No preselection, no provider ranking or self-preferencing. Wording comes from spec metadata. Only contracts verified at connection count.
- **Bindle floor (goes into extensions revision 3):**
  - no assignment or switch without an owner action;
  - no disclosure to an app of which other apps fill a field;
  - suggestions MAY be made, from verified contracts only.

  - The Messaging extension publishes a `connect` intent kind carrying a single-use invitation token.

- Signaling drops the `link` basis. Calls become Parlay call-invite messages carrying an `offer`.

## 2026-10-27 — Owner direction: invitation use cases, admission rules, lists, one-way links

**Owner direction (2026-10-27).**
- Single-use invitations suit person-to-person contact. Other cases also need covering, such as a contact link published on a website.
- Links need rules or automations: some auto-admit, some require accepting each invitee, some admit by rules.
- Contact lists are needed.
- One-way and two-way links are both needed, for example joining a newsletter without being able to message the owner.

**Coordinator proposal (provisional, unsigned; to fold into the contacts spike after its review).**
- **One invitation record in the messaging app, with five settings:**
  - uses (one, N, or unlimited);
  - expiry;
  - admission (automatic, review each, or rules);
  - direction ("can message you" two-way, or "receives from you only" one-way);
  - tags and lists to apply on joining.
- **Presets:** "Invite a person" (one use, two-way, automatic); "Website contact link" (unlimited, two-way, review or rules by default); "Newsletter/follow" (unlimited, one-way, always unsubscribable).
- **One-way links:** the subscriber's app allowlists the publisher, while the publisher's app records a subscriber without admitting inbound messages.
- **Lists are tags.** Allowlist entries carry provenance tags ("via link X").
- **One owner rules engine** (conditions to actions) serves both invitation admission and inbound message handling.
  - Conditions: via link, handle domain, organization membership, tag, body content.
  - Actions: admit, hold, tag, refuse, route.
- **Public-link safeguards:** per-link rate limits; review or rules as the public default; revocation offers "stop new joins" or "also remove everyone admitted via this link".
- **Spec boundary:**
  - Bindle Messaging specifies only the invitation intent data (token, inviter, offered direction), the redemption message and uniform result codes.
  - Uses, admission, rules, presets, tags and lists are Parlay features.
  - Nothing goes in core.

## 2026-10-27 — Owner direction: components declare `embed_url`, no hard-coded path

**Owner direction (2026-10-27).** The islands embed path should not be hard-coded.

**Coordinator decision (provisional, unsigned).**
- The embedded-components extension option becomes `embed_url`: a full HTTPS URL that the issuer declares, at any path.
- Every security check (postMessage target, frame-ancestors, the component-origin envelope, distinctness from the issuer and embedder origins) uses the origin of `embed_url`.
- That origin MUST serve only the provider's islands surface. The reason: browsers isolate by origin, not path, so any other content on it would hold island powers.
- Island parts and parameters are appended to the declared URL instead of to a fixed `/embed` path.

**Not yet applied.** The change goes in with the components extension migration (CR-X3-16), because `embed_origin` is used by packages/sdk (capabilities, testing), packages/federation/components-profile.mjs, apps/web/src/bl/authorize-entry-embed.mjs, the components profile, its descriptor JSON, auth.md, protocol.md and extensions.md.

## 2026-10-27 — Owner direction: keep `embed_origin`; islands document at the origin root

**Owner direction (2026-10-27).**
- Keep `embed_origin`, which supersedes the `embed_url` entry above. The security reason holds: the origin must serve nothing but the islands.
- Asked why the islands are not at the root.

**Coordinator decision (provisional, unsigned).**
- The embedded-components extension defines the island document as `<embed_origin>/?client=…#<part>.v<n>`, at the root.
- Every other path on the embed origin is provider-private: island assets, the service worker and the island's own API, none of which embedders ever address.
- The current `/embed` prefix was a 3sln.me implementation convenience, with no protocol reason behind it:
  - one Worker serves both hosts and uses the prefix to tell them apart (packages/runtime/routes/federation.mjs:213-233; http.mjs:37 refuses `/embed` on the main origin);
  - the service worker is scoped to `/embed/`.
- On a dedicated origin, routing by host instead is cleaner.
- Applied with the components extension migration (CR-X3-16): the profile text, packages/sdk/src/islands-protocol.mjs `islandURL`, the embed host routing, and the tests.

- An offer MAY omit its principal: an open offer admits any verified principal except the minting entity.
- An offer MAY admit `uses` from 1 to a provider maximum (default 1).
- Every offer has an expiry and is revocable. The expiry range is 10–900 s.
- **Service-class endpoints** are provider features, and apps of entities whose kind is not `person`. They MAY mint for up to 90 days, and they auto-accept their own offers on every endpoint of the minting app or feature.
- **Why 90 days:** it matches the default cross-entity pairing expiry, forces at least quarterly rotation of a publishable capability, and bounds both the damage of a leak and the time a stale offer holds a live-offer slot.
- **Why 900 s for open offers from a person's apps:** a person must never have a standing public address, which CL-10 rejected. 900 s still covers a code shown in person, or a group the app cannot list by principal.
- **Abuse bounds:**
  - a use is reserved atomically at admission, spent by the first claim and released on an unclaimed end;
  - per-offer, per-(principal, offer) and per-(issuer, offer) windows apply, plus the issuer and host-wide windows;
  - open-offer invites never use the pending reserve;
  - blocks apply first;
  - revocation ends pending sessions silently;
  - a dead offer looks exactly like an unknown one;
  - tokens are never logged;
  - every check is local and runs first at step 7.
- The approval page of a service-class handler discloses all of this.
- Owner question Q10 is rewritten against the owner's verbatim "app to app, user to user, provider to provider … all use cases" direction. New Q12 covers `none` reserved.

**Pairings (M1–M3, L7, L10; new SG-46).**
- At most one cross-entity pairing per (peer principal, kind line), in any state, enforced at creation.
- An app learns the pairings that cover it through `endpoints({endpoint})` `pairings` and a new `pairing` `listen` event, and learns nothing else about pairings.
- The M4 confirmation is reachable from the `peer` (interactive) side for every value of `opens`.
- Provider features are never pairing parties.
- Two P3 readings: activation at creation, and single-submit activation on an M5 enrolment page.
- P4 is spelled out for cross-entity pairings: listed with the local app and in a by-peer list.
- The confirmation code covers the provider-chosen `user_code`, so it cannot be ground offline.

**Messaging §5.5 (M5, L3, L4).**
- Alerting is allowed only if the receiving owner has sent the author a message in a two-party conversation, plus the existing expiry, state and rate rules. Nothing depends on list policies or CL-23.
- The call kind's `parties` is `other`.
- `expiresAt` ≤ the earliest embedded offer `expires_at` − 60 s. Offer entries now carry `expires_at`.
- A near-expiry dial-back that misses its offer is acknowledged.

**Appendix C (M6), checked against the code.**
- `packages/rtc/relay.mjs` imports `relay-credentials.mjs`, so that file is kept.
- There is no `beam-retirement.mjs`.
- `packages/runtime/account/contact-profile.mjs` has no imports, so its row is removed.
- `packages/core/signed-object.mjs` does not exist yet ("once created").
- `jws.mjs` and `tickets.mjs` import `packages/links/envelope.mjs` today.

**Readings and disagreements.**
- `endpoints` gains an optional `endpoint` argument.
- An `open` to another entity must carry a basis.
- A decline spends an offer use.
- `revoke_offer` with a token list covers the whole minting app.
- Reservation replaces spend-at-admission for every offer, not only open ones, so there is one rule. A bound offer whose first dial-back goes unanswered can now be used again before it expires.
- M1 is applied as "one pairing in any state", stricter than "one live", to avoid activation races.
- These are listed in §A.7 and stay provisional.

No code changed, so `npm test` was not run.

## 2026-10-27 — Recovery reissue: cancel from the replacing device (bug fix)

Provisional bug fix.

**Symptom.** `npm run test:recovery-reissue` timed out in the browser test that cancels the pending window. It was already failing at 10852e1; no script ran the file.

**Cause.**
- The "Cancel sessions" rule (re-verification follow-ups, 2026-10-23) ends the sessions that staged and confirmed the reissue.
- The view marks that same device `cancellable`, because its session predates the begin.
- When the owner cancelled from it, the console's follow-up `GET /api/account` hit 401. The confirmation was lost and the owner saw "Your session expired".

**Fix.**
- `reissueRecoveryCancel` returns `signedOut:true`, with no account projection, when the caller's session did not survive the cancel.
- `CancelPendingRecoveryReissue` then signs this browser out of the account and shows the outcome on the account picker (en/es) without sending another request.
- The browser test now expects this.

**Regressions.** `tests/identity-wargame2.test.mjs` and `tests/browser/recovery-reissue-window.mjs`. Each fails when its fix is reverted.

**Follow-up (coordinator, provisional).** Keep offering the cancel on the replacing device, since a stolen-session scenario may need it, but warn on the control that cancelling signs this device out. Queued.

## 2026-10-27 — signaling.v1 spec rev 3.2 (rev 3.1 verification fixes)

Provisional (coordinator), unsigned. Specification only: `docs/spec/signaling.md` (revision 3.2) and `docs/spec/messaging.md` §5.5. No code changed. Findings map to fixes in signaling Appendix A.8; decisions are SG-47 to SG-51, with SG-31 and SG-43 revised.

**Service offers (H1, L-8, L5; SG-47).**
- A service-class offer belongs to the minting app or feature, not to the minting endpoint.
  - Dial-backs route to every eligible and online endpoint of that app or feature. Online means a `listen` outstanding or within the liveness window (reference 60 s).
  - The first claim wins atomically.
- Other offers keep minting-endpoint routing. The online condition is scoped to service offers, because a sleeping person-app endpoint is woken by its doorbell.
- An offer ends only on:
  - revocation, or expiry;
  - the end of the minting app's or feature's authority for the kind;
  - removal of a service designation (offers over 900 s only);
  - the entity's move or deletion.
- Unregistering an endpoint never ends an offer, and neither does its expiry. Endpoint expiry is now a §14.2 trigger with the effects of `unregister`.
- A move kills published offers, and this is now stated for service operators.

**Open-offer abuse bounds (H2, M1; SG-48).**
- Open-offer invites are charged only to their own windows and the host-wide initiator window, never to windows that unbased traffic fills. Their own windows are:
  - per offer;
  - per (principal, offer);
  - a per-issuer fair share of max(W / (n + 1), F).
- Reference values are examples and remain provider policy:
  - for other offers: 60/h, 6/h and F 6/h;
  - for service offers: 3,600/h, 12/h and F 60/h.
- Operational responses are named: block providers, rotate the offer, mint per-audience offers.
- An open-offer sub-budget caps sessions admitted on open offers at half of pending capacity and half of connected capacity (reference).
- No offer admits, or takes a use, when its routing set is empty.

**Use accounting (M2, M4, L1; SG-49).**
- Bound offers are single-use again and spent at admission (`uses` absent or 1). This removes the rev 3.1 re-dial and polling leak, and §12.1 is reworded.
- An open offer's use is reserved at admission and spent only by an `accept`. A decline or an unclaimed end releases it.
- A service-class endpoint MAY decline automatically under its declared policy.
- A claim and the end of its offer are decided atomically at the first-claim authority.

**Service-class narrowed (M3, L3; SG-50).**
- Service-class now means two things only:
  - provider features;
  - the apps of organization entities whose owner explicitly designated them service entities, through a new owner setting with its own disclosure page. It is exported and listed in owner controls, and removing it is a narrowing trigger.
- Person apps are not service-class. Neither are undesignated organizations' apps (including those on members' devices) or member-context endpoints.
- Q10 is corrected: a person entity gets standing reachability only through a provider feature it explicitly enables.
- Service bound offers are capped at 7 days (reference). The approval and designation pages disclose them.

**Residuals and consistency (M5, L2, L4, L-6, L-7, C.2; SG-51).**
- Residual stated: one holder can exhaust a person app's short open offer with throwaway principals, and can watch availability while it lives. 900 s and the small `uses` stay as the bound.
- Accepted with justification: a person's app re-minting single-use bound offers amounts to a short pairing without the owner page. Forbidding it would be unenforceable, and each offer expires within 900 s.
- The holder provider keeps an offer token only in its outbox. It never logs the token and deletes it with the invite payload.
- `endpoints({endpoint})` is now used everywhere for `pairings`.
- Glare is scoped to pairing invites and same-app own-entity `target` invites.
- The Appendix C.2 flag plan no longer requires `INTENT_LINKS_ENABLED`.
- Q12 is reworded.

**Messaging §5.5.**
- At most 8 offer entries, and each principal is at most 256 bytes serialized. A compact 8-entry body is about 3.4 KiB, under the 4 KiB cap.
- The group-call alert rule is stated: it needs a two-party unlock with the author.
- The unlock persists until a block or a per-author owner clear. Muting does not clear it.
- The author is compared by origin principal.

**Readings (provisional, A.8).**
- The empty-routing-set rule applies to every offer.
- Accept-only spending applies to person open offers too.
- Removing a designation revokes only offers over 900 s.

**Verification.** A relative link and anchor check over `docs/spec/**` passes, apart from the pre-existing `../architecture/messaging-app.md#13-email-bridge-handoff` anchor. Site-root links were not checked. No code changed, so `npm test` was not run.

## 2026-10-27 — Extensions revision 3.2 code review fixes (provisional)

Provisional (coordinator), not signed off by the user. Fixed the code findings from the independent review of b7c04cc, locally and with flags off.
- **M1:** the 30-day revocation bound is dated from the last evaluation that saw the declaration valid (`seenAt`), not from when a loss was noticed. A suspension is revoked once 30 days old by the clock, before any resumption, including when the declaration comes back; clock jumps cannot revoke or resume early. A new account-alarm sweep (`connectionsFeatureSweep`, every 6 h while a grant is watched, armed on enable) applies loss, revocation and the owner notice with nobody reading. Residual: with no provider-level ledger, a loss can be dated up to one sweep interval early (errs towards revoking sooner); the notice is the local owner notice only.
- **M2:** the provider-feature manifest rows (`PROVIDER_FEATURE_ROWS`) are shared by the authority manifest and the account-side declarations port, with the same mounts.
- **M3:** `grant-more`/`configure` emitted only with incremental authorization mounted; spec side closed by revision 3.3 (EXT3-30).
- **M4:** the registrable-domain own-flow exclusion applies in the initial flow, in `inspect` and server-side in `approve`; values chosen before the flow are kept as a baseline.
- **M5:** account severance ends every `rtc/approval/` record.
- **M6:** legacy bus manifests are requestable only while EVENT_BUSES_ENABLED; a bus field's consumers must be a subset of its `slot.consumers`.
- **Lows:** declarations applied before announcing (L1); per-field announcement reset (L2); `bindle.grant` changes on reorder, purpose or ingress change with old-grant credentials revoked — this reading of "value change" is provisional (L3); revoked features never regranted without a fresh enable (L4); fragment-pin mismatch suspends (L5); unknown members outrank invalid (L7); audience endpoints compare by WHATWG serialisation per EXT3-32, plus the UUIDv5 tx test vector and `|` refusal (L8); a 5xx never advances ordered failover (L9); dead `chainOf` `supersedes` reader removed (L12, partly).
- The seeded chaos test now uses a spec-derived reference model and fails on the old code (seed 6).
- **Deferred:** L6 (no other field mutation requires `expectedRevision`), L10 (`approve-app` admission exemption, interim RTC), L11 (legacy brokered assignment reset), remaining L12 naming leftovers.

## 2026-10-28 — Signaling revision 3.2 engine: independent review fixes (H-1, M-1 to M-4, L-1 to L-3, L-6)

Provisional (coordinator), unsigned; flags stay default-off; local behaviour only.
- **H-1, connection end.** Ending a connection no longer depends on INTEGRATIONS_ENABLED or on a swallowed hook. The engine records the app's connection generation when the owner approves it (`sig/app/`); endpoints, approvals, offers and pairings of an ended or earlier connection admit, route and authorize nothing at once, and never revive after a reconnect. The tick sweeps stale apps (clearing, then §14.2), and re-approval clears first. `AppConnections.disconnect` calls a connection-ended hook. The cascade drain and `grantSync` no longer swallow failures; grantSync failures are retried from `grant-sync` rows on the federation cleanup alarm. Choice: any connection generation change counts as connection end for signaling, including pause/resume, re-setup and a manifest change (conservative over-narrowing beyond §20.1.4). Approvals with no recorded generation (e.g. imported) stay inert until re-approved.
- **M-1.** Contract result shaping keeps extra members only for pure maps, shapes `anyOf`/`oneOf` values by validate-then-copy, and the compiler supports `dependentRequired`. **Correction** to the engine-phase entry above: the shaping change did not restore preferences-v2 `values`; pinned preferences-v2 reads with non-empty `values` threw `artefact_unverifiable` until this fix, and the mixed `properties` plus `additionalProperties` case leaked members a later version may name. Both are now tested.
- **M-2.** Revoked and expired offers are deleted at once, and every offer scan is paged in full.
- **M-3.** **Correction** to the engine-phase entry above: the code capped pairings at all of base pending capacity, not half. It now caps them at half of base pending capacity, computed like the open-offer sub-budget, and the chaos model encodes the spec value.
- **M-4.** Member-context tokens carry `member` in the dispatch context, and their endpoints are never service-class (§4.3).
- **Lows.** Offer expiry, the 7-day pending pairing limit and pairing expiry are enforced at use (L-1); an own-entity pairing needs two different apps (L-2); an excluded handler cannot be approved and an existing approval of it is inert while excluded (L-3); relay, renew and send require an approval that admits the session's kind version (L-6).
- **Divergence (L-7).** Grant revocation also clears session handler approvals; §20.1.4 lists only connection end and manifest change.
- **Open.** L-4: `signalingClientSessionRevoked` is still uncalled (TODO; required before C.5 step 7). L-5: owner-page obligations recorded as a release gate in docs/3sln/release-gates.md ("Signaling").
- **Tests.** Engine tests for each fix, and a new spec-derived lifecycle chaos test (service-class offers, approval removal, app and grant revocation, connection end, expiry races, windows and capacity, own pairings, relay; the fair share and host-wide window are modelled but never bind with one issuer).
